chapter: Hightower: New Orleans parades and early players
title: Bunk Johnson as a boy and Buddy Bolden's band
summary: Hightower says Bunk began playing with Bolden's band as a child, living in his neighborhood.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Down near Clayborne and Dumaine, but it's an undertaking part. Yeah. Oh, one other question. Did you ever hear Bunk Johnson, did you ever hear him play?
Bunk Johnson? Why, Bunk, why, he started to play him. Bunk started to play him when Eddie Bolden had a band.
Yeah. Did you ever hear Bolden?

Oh, yes. But I was so small then, see. And his mother didn't want him to play. So Bolden and them begged his mother and they took him on a job. And Bolden used to bring his clothes for him to dress him. And take him back home and put him in his knee pants and send him home. He lived in my neighborhood at Pellis City and Cronolette.

When he was little. And his mother, he'd make his mother mad or something. When he was out there playing, she'd make him come in. We'd be out there playing Marvels in the street. He'd have to stamp on the fence and look at us. See. And he kept on, kept on until after he grew up. He still kept to that horn. When his mother got so that let him go. So he didn't stop uptown at all for no musicians. He went downtown. He got in with some band downtown. I don't know what that band was named. But Bunk come in and went out so quick until as I try to figure the music world as it's gone so poor today. I didn't hardly realize that Bunk had been in the music business until we just forgot it. Because he come up so, all of a sudden Bunk was the greatest trumpet player in the world. He really thought he was great. Then he went right down and he left New Orleans and went to somewhere as in Mississippi on a rice farm and stayed down there until Esquire. Got him. Well now I was to make that concert he made, Esquire made, see, in New York.
